**Acceptance Criteria:**

*The following should be defined and documented.*

- Positive functional scenarios
- Negative functional scenarios
- Out of Scope functional scenarios
- Monitoring (where applicable), Logs/Audit Trail, Observability, Scale, Performance and APIs Metrics
- Security Audit Complete
- Pass the ATA (Architectural Threat Analysis) – No Critical/High gaps, mitigation plan for medium and lows
- Meet the Pen Test Criteria – Use Armor tool – * Check with Matthew Yang on documentation to quantify (ex. No CAT1 findings, mitigation plan for CAT2/CAT3/etc.)
- Compliance Audit complete

**Definition of Done Checklist:  **

*PLMs are to work with Engineering to define and document some of these parameters and baselines. PLMs must ensure that all the 13 items have been met and signed off. (PI exit criteria for each epic)*

1. Monitoring against requirements
2. Logs/Audit trail requirements
3. Observability plan
4. Scale requirements
5. Performance metrics
6. APIs to expose
7. UX Designs
8. Security and Compliance
9. Complete Documentation (Engineering)
10. User guides documented and then reviewed by PLMs
11. Support decks should be created highlighting the goals, functional specs of the feature, the troubleshooting mechanisms, demo videos if UI is involved, escalation paths.
12. Demo presentations should be completed presented to the right audience
13. All testing should be completed (unit, load, integration, functional etc. what is applicable)
14. PLMs should follow the PLM best practices for the EPIC. (Refer to the Best Practices Guide)
